title: CurXecute: Cursor writes .cursor/mcp.json without approval and starts the server
summary: Cursor below 1.3.9 required approval to edit an existing dotfile but not to create one, so an indirect prompt injection delivered through a connected MCP server could write a new .cursor/mcp.json and have Cursor run the command it named. Aim Labs demonstrated it end to end through a crafted Slack message read by the Slack MCP server.
severity_rationale: Code execution on the developer machine from content the agent merely reads, with no approval step reached.
